source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A range of emotional responses, potentially including grief, anger, and gradual adaptation, similar to responses seen with other significant, life-altering changes","B":"Fairly little need for any ongoing psychosocial support once the client's physical rehabilitation phase has been fully completed and closed out","C":"A process that unfolds in an essentially identical, fully predictable way for every single client who happens to experience an injury like this one","D":"Immediate, complete acceptance of the injury, without any real emotional adjustment period needed in the weeks and months that follow the event"}}
source_row.rationale: Psychological adjustment to a new spinal cord injury often includes a range of emotional responses, potentially including grief, anger, and gradual adaptation over time, similar to responses seen with other significant, life-altering changes, warranting individualized nursing support that continues beyond the physical rehabilitation period alone.
